name: Šibenik
title: Holidays in Šibenik
intro: A stone city on the Dalmatian coast with a UNESCO cathedral, four fortresses and the waterfalls of Krka National Park nearby. Here's what Šibenik is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The stone façade of the Cathedral of St James in Šibenik
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are best, warm and great for Krka's waterfalls. July and August are hot and busy at the park. Spring brings full waterfalls.

things.name: Cathedral of St James
things.blurb: A UNESCO cathedral built entirely of stone, with 71 carved faces.

things.name: St Michael's Fortress
things.blurb: A fortress with views over the old town, used for summer concerts.

things.name: Barone Fortress
things.blurb: A fortress with an augmented-reality history tour.

things.name: Krka National Park
things.blurb: Waterfalls and boardwalks, about 20 minutes away.

things.name: Kornati islands
things.blurb: Boat trips to a national park of bare islands.

things.name: Old town lanes
things.blurb: Stone steps and alleys climbing from the waterfront.

faqs.question: Is Šibenik worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's less touristy than Split or Dubrovnik, with a real old town and Krka's waterfalls close by.

faqs.question: How do you get to Šibenik?
faqs.answer: Fly into Split, about 45 minutes away, or Zadar, about an hour. Both have direct flights from the UK.

faqs.question: Can you swim at Krka National Park?
faqs.answer: Not any more. Swimming at Skradinski Buk has been banned since 2021.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Šibenik?
faqs.answer: May, June and September, around 23 to 28°C.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Šibenik?
faqs.answer: Two or three days covers the city, Krka and a boat trip.
